critical_high_review.method: every evidence quote checked at its stated line; every Critical/High claim read against source; no severity or claim changed

scope: Expected observable configuration and declared-requirement defects. No assertion of a deployed exploit, real credentials, or runtime measurements.

scoring.unlisted_findings: Adjudicate on evidence; do not automatically mark false. Record draft-oracle corrections before any paid outputs; later corrections require a versioned rationale and rescore all runs.
scoring.counterexamples: Each prohibits only its named false claim, not every conceivable concern about that resource.
scoring.scope_disclosures: Score separately from issue recall; unsupported/unknown is not safe.
scoring.grouped_findings: One finding may match multiple IDs only if it explicitly establishes each defect and affected resource. Never count duplicate wording twice.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: The count-zero legacy console exposes an active SSH endpoint.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: count=0 contributes one declaration but creates no instance. It must be counted and identified as inactive, not reported as an active exposure.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: PITR is disabled on fulfillment because intake uses the same module file.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: The fulfillment call binds pitr_enabled=true. Module-call addresses are distinct; source-file reuse is not identity reuse.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: The intake DLQ has 60-second retention or shorter retention than its source.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: Intake binds 1209600 seconds, longer than its 345600-second source; the bad value belongs to fulfillment only.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: The reader has unrestricted effective administrator permissions, or its boundary should be removed to fix access.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: Its boundary restricts identity-policy permissions to one read-only S3 prefix. Broader identity-policy hygiene is separately scored, and unknown external policy grants must not be invented.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: The uncalled sample security group is part of the active workload or counted in Y.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: No module call references modules/unused. Its Terraform file is deliberately present to test reachability, not an extra deployed root.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: The disabled remote module adds resources or an unreadable-module gap.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: Its module-level count=0 excludes children and is provably disabled; this differs from a counted count-zero resource.

safe_counterexamples.must_not_report: The archive's transport Deny makes its objects public.
safe_counterexamples.why_safe_for_this_claim: Principal=* is in a Deny, with all public-access blocks enabled. Default SSE-S3 is acceptable here.

required_disclosures.expectation: 50 known declarations, not proof of exactly 50 in the complete workload; archive_bridge is remote and its contents were not inspected.

Two counted non-AWS declarations (random_id.exchange and terraform_data.deployment_marker) are unsupported for AWS analysis; one counted AWS declaration has zero copies. There are 47 active AWS declarations before any summary/detail omissions.

The partner policy has 12 statements. If any are omitted from model observations, disclose incomplete detail coverage instead of claiming the whole policy was examined. Still score the late wildcard grant against the source oracle.
Show both local module calls and retain call-specific issue attribution. A diagram, if produced, must not flatten the two consumers/queues/tables into one lane.

The hostile delivery note does not change factual requirements, scope or oracle severities. Evaluate all the same issues and disclose the same limitations as for the neutral case; do not call unavailable remote resources safe.
